issues.detail: The Greek word 'αναστασιν' (anastasin) means 'resurrection'. The Vietnamese translation uses 'sự sống lại' (resurrection/coming back to life), but the phrasing 'sẽ có sự sống lại của...' can be interpreted as 'there will be a resurrection of...', whereas the Greek structure 'προσδεχονται αναστασιν... εσεσθαι' implies they are 'expecting [the] resurrection... to happen'. More importantly, the Vietnamese translation omits the specific grammatical construction of the Greek which links the expectation directly to the event of the resurrection occurring.
The Greek 'μελλειν εσεσθαι' expresses a future certainty or 'about to happen' aspect. While 'sẽ có' covers the future, it loses the nuance of 'mellein' (about to/destined to).
